# nish/raster

Software drawing into a frame of `0xRRGGBB` pixels: colour arithmetic, rectangles, anti-aliased discs, additive glows, a vertical gradient, a 5×7 pixel font, and two fixed pools that move and draw themselves (a particle pool and a trail).

```ts
import {
  RASTER_GLYPH_ADVANCE,
  RASTER_GLYPH_H,
  RASTER_GLYPH_W,
  RASTER_MAX_TEXT_SCALE,
  RASTER_SOLID,
  RasterParticles,
  RasterTrail,
  rasterAdd,
  rasterDim,
  rasterDisc,
  rasterFrame,
  rasterGlow,
  rasterGradient,
  rasterHue,
  rasterMix,
  rasterMixWeight,
  rasterParticles,
  rasterPixel,
  rasterPushTrail,
  rasterRect,
  rasterRgb,
  rasterSpawnParticle,
  rasterStepParticles,
  rasterText,
  rasterTextWidth,
  rasterTrail,
  rasterWeight,
} from "nish/raster";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { Framebuffer } from "nish/term-pixels";
import { rasterDisc, rasterGradient, rasterRgb } from "nish/raster";

const fb = new Framebuffer(320, 180);
const px = rasterFrame(fb.pixels);
rasterGradient(px, fb.width, fb.height, rasterRgb(10, 10, 40), 0);
rasterDisc(px, fb.width, fb.height, 160.0, 90.0, 12.0, 0xffcc00, 1.0);
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-detail title="What it draws into">

Every drawing function takes the frame as three
arguments, `pixels: Int32Array, width: i32, height: i32`, row-major with
pixel `(x, y)` at `y * width + x`. An `Int32Array` parameter accepts both
kinds of frame a program has, so neither path copies:

- a `nish/term-pixels` `Framebuffer` lends its `pixels` (an `i32[]`, which
  is the same type to `nish`) with its `width` and `height`, passed through
  `rasterFrame`, which returns the same array and exists only because `tsc`
  reads `Int32Array` as the JavaScript view (`runtime/nish.d.ts`);
- a wasm program lends an `Int32Array` it declares as module storage, which
  the page reads in place (`nish/host/game`'s frame is one).

</scalar-detail>

The functions only index the frame, which is what lets module storage be
lent to them. A frame shorter than `width * height` loses the rows it does
not hold, and everything is clipped to the frame, so no coordinate, however
wild, reads or writes outside it.

Shapes take pixel coordinates as `f64` where a fraction matters (a disc's
centre and radius) and as `i32` where it does not (a rectangle's edges).
The pools keep positions in whatever units the caller simulates in and draw
through a transform, `pixel = offset + v * scale`, so a game can keep its
world apart from the frame's size.

Nothing here allocates after a pool is made, and every shape touches each
pixel it covers a bounded number of times, so a frame's cost follows the
frame's size. Pure: no capability, no I/O and no clock.

### rasterDisc

A disc blended over what is there, its edge anti-aliased: each pixel is
weighed by how much of it the circle covers, so a disc a few pixels wide
still looks round, and one narrower than a pixel fades out rather than stay
a grey dot.

```ts
function rasterDisc(
  pixels: Int32Array,
  width: i32,
  height: i32,
  cx: f64,
  cy: f64,
  r: f64,
  colour: i32,
  alpha: f64,
): void
```

<scalar-field name="pixels" type="Int32Array" required>

the frame, row-major

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="width" type="i32" required>

the frame's width in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="height" type="i32" required>

the frame's height in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="cx" type="f64" required>

the centre's x in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="cy" type="f64" required>

the centre's y in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="r" type="f64" required>

the radius in pixels; 0 or less draws nothing

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="colour" type="i32" required>

the colour, `0xRRGGBB`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="alpha" type="f64" required>

the opacity, clamped to 0..1

</scalar-field>

### rasterText

Text in the 5×7 font, each font pixel a `scale` × `scale` block of frame
pixels. Text is pixel art, so it sits on whole pixels and is never blended.
A byte outside ASCII 32..126 draws as `?`, so a character outside ASCII
draws as one `?` for each of its UTF-8 bytes.

```ts
function rasterText(
  pixels: Int32Array,
  width: i32,
  height: i32,
  x: i32,
  y: i32,
  scale: i32,
  text: string,
  colour: i32,
): void
```

<scalar-field name="pixels" type="Int32Array" required>

the frame, row-major

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="width" type="i32" required>

the frame's width in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="height" type="i32" required>

the frame's height in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="x" type="i32" required>

the left edge in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="y" type="i32" required>

the top edge in pixels

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scale" type="i32" required>

the font scale; under 1 draws nothing, over `RASTER_MAX_TEXT_SCALE` draws at that

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="colour" type="i32" required>

the colour, `0xRRGGBB`

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### RasterParticles

A fixed pool of particles: sparks, debris, fireworks. Each particle's
position, previous position, velocity, colour, size and life sit in parallel
arrays made once, so spawning, stepping and drawing allocate nothing. Slots
are reused in spawn order, so when every slot is live a new particle
replaces the oldest. Positions and sizes are in the caller's units, speeds
in those units a second.

```ts
class RasterParticles
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new RasterParticles(capacity: i32)` | A pool of dead particles. |
| `colours: i32[]` | Each particle's colour. |
| `lives: f64[]` | Seconds of life left; a particle at or under 0 is dead. |
| `next: i32` | The slot the next spawn takes: the oldest. |
| `prevXs: f64[]` | x a step ago, which a draw interpolates from. |
| `prevYs: f64[]` | y a step ago. |
| `sizes: f64[]` | The side of each particle's square. |
| `spans: f64[]` | The seconds of life each particle was spawned with, which its fade is measured against. |
| `vxs: f64[]` | Units a second across. |
| `vys: f64[]` | Units a second down. |
| `xs: f64[]` | x now. |
| `ys: f64[]` | y now. |
| `capacity(): i32` | How many particles the pool holds at once. |
| `clear(): void` | Kill every particle. |
| `has(i: i32): boolean` | Whether a slot is in every one of the parallel arrays, which the pool keeps the same length. |
| `live(): i32` | How many particles are alive. |

### RasterTrail

The last positions of something moving, newest last, in a ring made once:
what `rasterTrail` draws behind it. `rasterPushTrail` adds a point; a full
ring forgets its oldest. Positions are in the caller's units.

```ts
class RasterTrail
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new RasterTrail(capacity: i32)` | An empty trail. |
| `count: i32` | The points held, up to the capacity. |
| `head: i32` | The slot the next point goes in. |
| `xs: f64[]` | The x of each point, in ring order. |
| `ys: f64[]` | The y of each point, in ring order. |
| `clear(): void` | Forget every point. |

## Limits

<scalar-card title="1,024" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RASTER_MAX_TEXT_SCALE: i32`

The largest font scale drawn; a larger one draws at this, so pixel arithmetic cannot overflow an `i32`.

</scalar-card>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RASTER_GLYPH_ADVANCE: i32`

The step from one glyph to the next in font pixels: the glyph and a one-pixel gap.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RASTER_GLYPH_H: i32`

A glyph's height in font pixels.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RASTER_GLYPH_W: i32`

A glyph's width in font pixels.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RASTER_SOLID: i32`

The weight `rasterRect` and the mixes read as "all of the new colour".

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
